Substitute $x = 4$, $y = 5$ into each equation.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{RHS} &= 3(4)-7 \\ &= 5 \\ &= \text{LHS} \end{aligned}$$
For $x-2y+6=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{LHS} &= 4-2(5)+6 \\ &= 0 \\ &= \text{RHS} \end{aligned}$$
The point satisfies both equations.

$\therefore$ Yes, the student is correct.

parts.latex:
The solution for the pair of simultaneous equations $3x - 2y = 12$ and $2x + 5y = -11$ has the value of $x$ equal to 2.

What is the value of $y$?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $x = 2$ into $3x - 2y = 12$.
$$\begin{aligned} 3(2) - 2y &= 12 \\ 6 - 2y &= 12 \\ -2y &= 6 \\ y &= -3 \end{aligned}$$
Check in $2x + 5y = -11$:
$$2(2) + 5(-3) = 4 - 15 = -11$$
$$\therefore\ y = -3 \text{ (option A)}$$

parts.latex:
A company's Costs ($\$C$) and Income ($\$I$) from sales are represented by the equations:

$$C = 2500 + 15n \quad \text{and} \quad I = 25n$$

Let $n$ be the number of items sold.

Which statement is correct when 200 items are sold?

solutions.latex:
For $n=200$ items, find the cost and the income.
$$\begin{aligned} C &= 2500+15\times 200 = \$5500 \\ I &= 25\times 200 = \$5000 \end{aligned}$$
Profit $= I - C$:
$$\begin{aligned} I-C &= 5000-5500 \\ &= -\$500 \end{aligned}$$
The income is less than the cost, so the company makes a loss of $\$500$ (option B).

Two students Jaylon and Milan run 60m at a constant speed.

Jaylon begins to run five seconds after Milan.

The equations representing the graphs of the two students' runs are:

Jaylon: $D = 3t - 15$ Milan: $D = 2t$ where $D$ is the distance ran and $t$ is the time after Milan begins running

figures.cap: blank grid: distance (metres) 0-80 against time (seconds) 0-35
solution sketch: lines D=3t-15 and D=2t drawn on the grid, intersecting at (15, 30)

Who was the faster runner? Justify your answer with suitable calculations.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{1265_q30_s1}

The lines intersect at $(15, 30)$. At this point the two runners are the same distance, $30$ m, from the start.
criteria: Draws both lines correctly, or equivalent merit
Draws one line correctly, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source rubric (1 for each line, 1 for explanation) rewritten top-down.

solutions.latex:
Jaylon runs $60$ m when $D = 60$.
$$\begin{aligned} 60 &= 3t - 15 \\ 3t &= 75 \\ t &= 25 \end{aligned}$$
He started $5$ seconds after Milan.
$$\text{Time} = 25 - 5 = 20 \text{ seconds}$$

Compare average speeds, taken at the intersection point $(15, 30)$.

Jaylon ran $30$ m in $15 - 5 = 10$ s, and Milan ran $30$ m in $15$ s.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Jaylon's average speed} &= \dfrac{30}{10} = 3 \text{ m/s} \\ \text{Milan's average speed} &= \dfrac{30}{15} = 2 \text{ m/s} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Jaylon is the faster runner.}$$
